summary: Iteration 3 backend verification — added /app/backend/tests/test_admin_master_auth.py with 13 new tests covering master-admin login, brute-force lockout, restart-safe seeding, and Free-tier credit refresh. Full suite: 53 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed (KNOWN BUG). All iteration_1/2 tests still pass. Verified: (a) POST /api/auth/admin-master/login with correct creds → 200, user.role='admin', user.email='master@admin.local', session_token starts with 'vtp_m_', HttpOnly cookie set; (b) returned token gates /api/auth/me (role=admin) and /api/admin/stats; (c) wrong password and wrong username both return 401 'Invalid credentials' with identical detail (timing uses bcrypt on both arms); (d) master_admin settings doc persisted with bcrypt $2b$ hash; master user row exists with role=admin, plan=studio; idempotent re-login works (different session tokens); (e) Free-plan user with last_credit_refresh=48h ago is refilled to 2 credits on next /auth/me call; refresh skipped within 24h; pro-plan user is never auto-refilled; (f) runtime_config.get_gemini_key() precedence verified by code review: admin override → GEMINI_API_KEY env → EMERGENT_LLM_KEY (correct).

critical.issue: Lockout is BYPASSABLE in production. _attempts bucket key is (request.client.host, username) but behind Kubernetes ingress request.client.host = the ingress pod IP. With ≥2 ingress replicas, fail attempts get distributed across multiple bucket keys (confirmed in backend logs: alternating 10.79.131.92 / 10.79.131.93 from the SAME test client). 5+ consecutive bad logins from one real user are split into 2-3 per bucket and never trigger the 429. Fix: in routers/admin_master_auth.py:master_login, read X-Forwarded-For (leftmost) for ip OR — since this is the single master account — drop ip from the key entirely (`key = req.username`) so it is a global per-username counter. Test currently marked xfail with this RCA in the docstring.

minor.issue: No 'free' plan is returned in /payments/plans — only paid tiers (starter, pro, studio, pack_50, …). The user-facing 'Free / 2 credits per day' messaging lives in frontend copy + the backend refresh_free_credits_if_due() logic. There is no API contract exposing the daily-credit number, so any future change to that number cannot be reflected automatically on the pricing page. Consider exposing free-tier metadata (daily_credits=2, plan='free') via /payments/plans or a new /pricing endpoint.

Cookie is set with samesite='none', secure=True, httponly=True — fine for cross-site preview-domain auth, but in same-origin production deployments samesite='lax' is the safer default. Currently fine because the frontend is served from a different subdomain than backend in the preview env.

In-memory brute-force tracker uses a plain dict (defaultdict) with no upper bound and no cleanup of stale entries except inside _is_locked_out. An attacker who keeps cycling unique usernames could grow the dict unbounded. Recommend periodic GC or a TTL-bounded cache (e.g., cachetools.TTLCache).

action_items: HIGH: Fix brute-force lockout key in routers/admin_master_auth.py to either (a) honour X-Forwarded-For (left-most) when computing ip, or (b) drop ip from the bucket key and use per-username global counter. Current behavior is BYPASSABLE behind k8s ingress (confirmed via backend logs and via reproducible xfail test).
Consider exposing free-tier daily_credits (2) via the /payments/plans response so the pricing page can read it from the API instead of hard-coding.
Add bounded TTL/GC to _attempts dict to prevent unbounded growth from username-cycling attackers.

Carried over from iteration_2 (still open): wrap emergentintegrations.send_message in asyncio.to_thread() to stop blocking the event loop during AI generation (causes transient 502 on concurrent polls).

The xfail test_lockout_after_5_failures will FLIP TO PASS once main agent fixes the ip-resolution in routers/admin_master_auth.py — at that point, change @pytest.mark.xfail to a plain test. Reproduction of the bug is documented in the test's xfail reason and in the rca field below. Backend logs at /var/log/supervisor/backend.*.log show the two distinct ingress IPs (10.79.131.92 and 10.79.131.93) servicing alternating requests from the same test client — this is the smoking gun. rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout bypass — RCA: _attempts dictionary in routers/admin_master_auth.py is keyed by f'{ip}:{username}' where ip = request.client.host. In the K8s preview environment (and any prod with a reverse proxy/ingress), request.client.host is the IP of the ingress pod that proxied the request — NOT the IP of the real end user. Backend logs prove that requests from a single test client are alternating between 10.79.131.92 and 10.79.131.93 (two ingress replicas), so 5 consecutive bad-password attempts from the same attacker are split into 2-3 entries per bucket, never reaching the 5-attempt threshold. Result: an attacker can perform unlimited password guesses against the master admin account. Reproduction: run pytest /app/backend/tests/test_admin_master_auth.py::TestMasterAdminLockout — fails 100% on the preview deployment. Fix options: (1) Use the canonical reverse-proxy header X-Forwarded-For: `ip = request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for','').split(',')[0].strip() or (request.client.host if request.client else '?')`. (2) Since this is a single master account, drop the ip from the bucket key and use only the username — gives a global per-account counter that cannot be bypassed by IP rotation. Recommend (2) for defense-in-depth, optionally combined with (1). After fix, the test should immediately pass without any other changes.
